task.title: Weak Signal
task.shortdesc: Identify and correct conditions that cause a weak Wi-Fi signal in one or more areas of the home.

prereq.p: Before you troubleshoot a weak Wi-Fi signal, make sure that:

ul.li: The is turned on and connected to the Internet.
The affected client device is connected to .
Wi-Fi is enabled on the affected client device.
The router antennas are installed correctly, if applicable.
You have recorded recent changes to the router location, wireless configuration, or network environment.

prereq.note: Make one change at a time. Test the Wi-Fi signal after each change.

context.p: Wi-Fi signal strength can decrease because of distance, physical obstructions, wireless interference, router placement, antenna orientation, or client-device limitations.
A weak signal can reduce network performance, cause connection delays, or disconnect a client device.
context.note: The number of Wi-Fi bars on a client device provides only a general indication of signal strength. Test the connection in the location where you normally use the device.
Record the signal level, noise level, signal-to-noise ratio, band, channel, and connected access point before you change the wireless configuration.

step.cmd: Determine where the Wi-Fi signal is weak.

substep.cmd: Check the signal on the affected client device near the .
Check the signal again in the affected location.
Test another wireless device in the same locations.

ul.li: If only one device has a weak signal, check the device Wi-Fi adapter, software, and network settings.
If multiple devices have a weak signal in one location, check the distance, physical obstructions, and interference.
If multiple devices have a weak signal in all locations, check the router placement, configuration, and antennas.

step.stepresult: The test identifies whether the problem affects one device, one location, or the complete coverage area.

step.cmd: Move the affected client device closer to the .

info.p: Keep the client device connected to while you move it.

step.cmd: Test the Wi-Fi connection near the router.

info.p: If the signal improves, distance or a physical obstruction is probably reducing the signal in the original location.
If the signal remains weak near the router, restart the client device and continue with the router checks.

step.stepresult: The test determines whether distance contributes to the weak signal.

step.cmd: Check the location of the router.

info.p: Make sure that the router is:

ul.li: Near the center of the required coverage area
On a stable and elevated surface
Outside a closed cabinet or drawer
Away from heat, water, and direct sunlight
Away from equipment that can cause interference

info.p: For more information, see .

step.cmd: Reduce physical obstructions between the router and the affected client device.

info.p: The following obstructions can reduce the Wi-Fi signal:

ul.li: Aquariums and other large containers of water

info.p: Move the router or client device to provide a clearer signal path.

info.note: Test the Wi-Fi signal before and after you move or turn off a potential source of interference.

step.cmd: Test the client device on another Wi-Fi band.

choices.choice: Use the 2.4 GHz band when the device is far from the router or behind several physical obstructions.
Use the 5 GHz band when the device is near the router and requires increased network performance.

info.p: The supports .

step.stepresult: The test identifies the band that provides a more reliable signal in the affected location.

step.cmd: Check the router antennas, if applicable.

substep.cmd: Make sure that each antenna is fully connected.
Check each antenna for visible damage.
Position each antenna as specified in the installation instructions.

info.note: Do not force the beyond its permitted movement range.

info.p: After the restart, reconnect the device to and test the signal again.

step.cmd: Restart the router if the weak signal continues.

substep.cmd: Use the restart control in the if it is available.
Wait until the router status indicators show normal operation.

info.note: Do not press the reset button. A factory reset can remove the custom network configuration.

step.cmd: Check the access point or mesh node used by the affected client device.

info.note: Do not put a mesh node in an area where the existing Wi-Fi signal is unusable. Put the node between the router and the area with a weak signal.

info.p: Sign in to the and open the .
Confirm that the or has a reliable connection to the home network.
If the mesh node has a weak connection, move it closer to the main router or another connected mesh node.
Review the following values when available:

ul.li: Connected access point or mesh node

info.note: The Wi-Fi indicator on a client device does not provide a standardized signal measurement. Use measured values when you compare coverage locations.

info.p: Use a wireless analysis tool or the available information in the to identify nearby networks and congested channels.
Keep automatic channel selection enabled when wireless conditions change frequently.
If manual channel selection is necessary, select a permitted channel with low utilization.
info.note: Do not use in every environment without evaluating local wireless conditions and applicable regional requirements.

info.p: Confirm that the router, access point, or mesh node uses a transmit-power level that provides the required coverage.
Do not automatically select the highest available transmit-power level. Excessive transmit power can increase interference and affect roaming between wireless coverage points.
info.note: Change transmit power only after you measure the coverage and interference conditions.

info.p: Use the firmware update function in the or get approved firmware from the .
info.note: Do not turn off the router during a firmware update.
Install only firmware intended for and the applicable .

step.cmd: Extend Wi-Fi coverage if the signal remains weak in the required area.

choices.choice: Use the when an Ethernet connection is available near the affected area.
Use the when multiple areas require additional coverage.

info.p: For more information, see .

step.cmd: Verify the Wi-Fi signal in the affected location.

substep.cmd: Put the client device in its normal use location.
Confirm that the device shows a stable Wi-Fi connection.
Confirm that the connection remains active during normal network use.

info.note: Record the signal level, band, channel, throughput, latency, and packet loss. Compare the results with the initial measurements.

step.stepresult: The client device has a stable Wi-Fi connection in the required coverage area.

result.p: The Wi-Fi signal provides stable connectivity in the required coverage area.

postreq.p: If the signal remains weak, collect the following information:

ul.li: The number and type of physical obstructions
The connected access point or mesh node
The measured signal level, noise level, channel utilization, throughput, latency, and packet loss

postreq.note: Do not send Wi-Fi passwords, administrator passwords, account passwords, or other confidential credentials to technical support.
